pairs.why: A's long, see-through ribbon tentacles trail diagonally like the real jellyfish, while B's frills are bunched up and more solid.
B is a plain navy light on a bracket like the real card, while A adds hinged side flaps the real light doesn't have.
A's yellow plastic caps and stripe look like a toy, while B keeps the real card's dark metal and bracket.
Both are drawn almost the same way, but B's level truss with a single stem mount above the light is a little closer to how the real card is built.
B's shapes are cleaner, with a bolder green and smoother finish closer to the real card, while A has more paper texture and fussier detail.
B's thick, shiny, puffy plastic edges look like a statue, while A's flatter, matte sheets are closer to the real card.
B has the real card's clean white border around flat green sheets, while A uses wavy, old-paper edges.
B matches the real card's tilted view with the underside showing and its thin pole, with a calmer finish, while A is a glossy, blown-up dome on a thick pole.
